standard_prerequisites.name: Cocones under a span
standard_prerequisites.statement: A cocone under a span (A <-f- C -g-> B) with vertex D is a triple (i,j,h) with i : A -> D, j : B -> D and h : prd z:C i(f z) = j(g z).
standard_prerequisites.use: The statement is about the two ways of transporting such a triple along t : D -> E.

standard_prerequisites.name: Maps of spans and their action on cocones
standard_prerequisites.statement: A map of spans (alpha,beta,gamma,phi,psi) acts on cocones by composing the legs and filling the square with the composite displayed in the author's numbered equation.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both composites in the statement go through that action, and the proof compares the two induced homotopies.

standard_prerequisites.name: ap preserves path concatenation
standard_prerequisites.statement: ap t of a composite of paths is the composite of the aps.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the last step of the proof at source line 974.

core_obligations: Fix (i,j,h) : cocone(D',D) and observe that both composites in the diagram have first two components t o i o alpha and t o j o beta, so only the homotopies have to be compared (source lines 953-954).
For the top-right composite, write the homotopy as the author's numbered composite with (i,j,h) replaced by (t o i, t o j, ap t o h), and display it explicitly (source lines 955-963).
For the left-bottom composite, write the homotopy as ap t applied to the original composite (source line 965).
Use that ap t respects path concatenation to identify the two composites term by term, and the identities ap t o ap i = ap (t o i) and likewise for j to finish (source lines 966-974).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the diagram to a comparison of the two induced homotopies.
Compare them using the functoriality of ap.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 7.4.10 at source lines 941-951: for any map of spans (alpha,beta,gamma,phi,psi) and any t : D -> E the square comparing the two ways of acting on cocones commutes. The statement is a diagram of function types between cocone types, and its proof (source lines 952-975) is a componentwise comparison rather than a formal consequence: both composites must first be unfolded to homotopies, the first being the author's numbered composite with (i,j,h) replaced by (t o i, t o j, ap t o h) (source lines 955-963), and the second being ap t applied to the original composite (source line 965); the identification then runs through the respect of ap for path concatenation and the two identities ap t o ap i = ap (t o i) and the analogue for j (source lines 966-974). The statement shows only the square.
